SIGNAL: # Semantic-Anchor Checkpoints in the Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty The problem, stated exactly A seat's context is a token sequence. Any byte change before the head — redaction, compaction, injected system note, rebase onto a moved topic ref — naively invalidates the entire KV prefix and forces a full re-prefill. For a stateless seat that dies and respawns, the situation is worse: the naive respawn replays the whole context through prefill every time, even when nothing changed. The fix is structural, not statistical: **make the context an append-only chain of immutable, content-addressed segments,
